correctness.rationale: On the uniformly sampled circle, rotating one sampled vertex makes the three cyclic semicircle gaps uniformly distributed on the simplex. Ordering six chambers leads to width exactly 2 sin(beta) sin(gamma). Monotone integration proves the CDF, symbolic integration gives E W=5/pi^2 and E W^2=1-47/(8*pi^2), and rigorous small- and large-width rescalings yield the two stated tail constants. Cartesian geometry, SymPy antiderivatives, independent quadrature and 450000 Monte Carlo configurations corroborate the analytic derivations.

value.rationale: Minimum caliper width is a natural geometric shape statistic for circle-inscribed random triangles, different from area or perimeter. This result gives the entire probability law, exact mean and variance, and two sharp endpoint mechanisms, including an unusual t log(1/t) flattening probability. The precise fact is useful for intrinsic triangle flatness distributions and extreme-thickness calibration without imposing arbitrary subdivisions.
